samples.summary: Deleting login-callback.test.ts leaves the CLI login callback server with zero tests, including the newly changed acceptance behavior
samples.evidence: This delta deletes packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts (the only test that ever exercised startCallbackServer) and un-exports the function (login.ts:153). The handler at login.ts:168-183 still has behavior worth pinning: 404 for a non-/callback path, 400 for a missing `code`, and — newly — accepting whatever `code` arrives with no state/nonce binding at all. I grepped the whole cli test dir for `startCallbackServer` (only hit was the deleted file) and globbed packages/cli/test/** — there is no other login/oauth test. Removing a feature's test along with the feature is legitimate, but the reverted behavior ("first code on the port wins") ships with no test asserting it either way, so a future re-introduction or regression of the callback contract is invisible to the suite. (The security merit of the revert itself is the security lens's call, not mine.)

samples.summary: No test pins the precedence order inside the new messageText chain (nested error.message vs top-level message)
samples.evidence: formatter.ts now resolves the message as `messageText(fields.message) ?? messageText(body?.message) ?? messageText(raw) ?? fallback.message`. The three new tests each exercise exactly one arm in isolation: 404 body has only a top-level `message` (line 277), the validation body only an array `message` (296), the 403 body only a bare `error` string (310). No test supplies a body carrying BOTH a nested `error.message` and a different top-level `message`, so swapping the first two arms of the chain — the one ordering decision the change actually makes — would keep the whole suite green. Same for an array under `fields.message` (a hand-built `{ error: { message: [...] } }` body), which is reachable through messageText but untested.

samples.summary: messageText's rejection paths (empty string, array of non-strings, object message) are untested
samples.evidence: messageText explicitly filters empty strings and non-string array members and returns undefined for other types, but output.test.ts only feeds it a non-empty string, an all-string array, and an absent value. A body like `{ message: '' }` or `{ message: [{}] }` or `{ message: { detail: 'x' } }` — all plausible from a proxy or a hand-rolled endpoint — has no test asserting it falls back to the caller's `HTTP <status>` message rather than emitting `""` or `[object Object]`.

finding.summary: New nonce plumbing in `GitHubAuthGuard` (query capture + 1..128 length bound) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The guard now reads `req.query.nonce` and stores it only when `typeof nonce === 'string' && length > 0 && length <= MAX_NONCE_LENGTH` (github-auth.guard.ts:26-38). There is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` — `ls packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts` yields auth.controller, cli-auth.store, auth.service, jwt.strategy, github.strategy only — and a repo-wide grep for `GitHubAuthGuard` in tests returns nothing. The controller spec exercises the echo by calling `cliAuthStore.createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y')` directly (auth.controller.spec.ts:220), bypassing the guard entirely. So the middle link of the chain (browser query → stored state) is untested: dropping the nonce read, inverting the length check, or accepting an array-valued `?nonce=` would keep every suite green.

verdict.reason: The behavior the finding says is untested does not exist in this repository. github-auth.guard.ts (full 31-line file) has no nonce handling: canActivate reads only req.query.mode and req.query.port, validates the port range, and calls cliAuthStore.createState(mode, portNum) with two arguments (line 24). There is no req.query.nonce read, no MAX_NONCE_LENGTH constant, and no 1..128 length bound. CliAuthStore.createState is declared as (mode: string, port: number) (cli-auth.store.ts:21-24) and StateEntry is {csrf, mode, port, expiresAt} (lines 4-9), so there is no nonce field to plumb or store. The reviewer's quoted test evidence is also inaccurate: auth.controller.spec.ts:192 is `cliAuthStore.createState('cli', 9876)` with two args, not `createState('cli', 9876, 'n0nce-x/y')` at line 220. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `nonce` matches only pnpm-lock.yaml, packages/docs/src/spell/dict/en_US.dic, and docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-sandbox-recipe.md — nothing in packages/backend; a grep for MAX_NONCE_LENGTH|GitHubAuthGuard|__cliStateToken across packages/ returns only the guard definition, auth.module.ts registration, auth.controller.ts usage, and github.strategy.ts:59. Since the described nonce feature is absent, there is no new/changed behavior shipped without coverage, so nothing blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: No test asserts the CLI actually sends `&nonce=` on the OAuth start URL it later gates on
finding.evidence: login.ts:42-46 mints the nonce and appends `&nonce=<enc>` to the OAuth URL; the callback server then rejects any callback that does not echo it (login.ts:206). The only new CLI test, test/login-callback.test.ts, calls `startCallbackServer('the-nonce')` in isolation and never drives `registerLoginCommand`'s action. If the `&nonce=` param were dropped or misnamed, the backend would echo no `state`, the CLI would 400 its own genuine callback and hang until the 30s timeout — and both the new CLI test and the backend controller test (which seeds the nonce into the store directly) would still pass.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise does not exist in this repository. I read packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts in full (271 lines): the OAuth URL is built at line 36 as `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` with no `nonce` parameter; lines 42-46 are the `open(oauthUrl)` try/catch, not nonce minting; `startCallbackServer` is declared at line 153 with ZERO parameters and invoked at line 33 as `startCallbackServer()`; and the callback handler (lines 168-227) validates only the `/callback` pathname and the presence of `code`, with no state/nonce comparison anywhere (the file ends at line 270, and line 206 is CSS inside the success HTML). A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `nonce` (excluding pnpm-lock.yaml) yields no hits in any packages/cli source or test file — only a spellcheck dictionary, an unrelated design-editor doc, and prior review artifacts. The claimed test file packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts does not exist; I enumerated all 25 files under packages/cli/test/. Furthermore, the CLI never mints or transmits a nonce at all: the state token is created server-side in packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:21-26, where the guard detects `mode=cli&port=<port>` and calls `cliAuthStore.createState(...)`, so the described failure mode (CLI 400-ing its own genuine callback because `&nonce=` was dropped or misnamed) is unreachable. This is not an untested behavior — it is a non-existent behavior, so there is no missing-test defect to block the merge gate under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: Nonce-mismatch coverage only exercises the length-differs branch, so a length-only comparison would pass
finding.evidence: `nonceMatches` (login.ts:164-169) is `a.length === b.length && timingSafeEqual(a, b)`. The test's two rejection cases are no state at all and `state=guessed` (7 chars) against `the-nonce` (9 chars) — both short-circuit on the length check, so `timingSafeEqual` is never reached with a mismatching same-length value. Replacing the body with `return a.length === b.length` (accepting any 9-char attacker state) leaves the suite green. A same-length wrong-value case (e.g. `state=xxx-nonce`) is what would pin the actual comparison.

verdict.reason: The finding's subject does not exist in this repository. (1) packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts is absent: the full listing of packages/cli/test/ has 25 files, none login-related, and the string "login-callback" occurs only inside .agent-review/correctness/*.json review artifacts. (2) There is no nonceMatches helper: a repo-wide grep for nonceMatches|timingSafeEqual matches only packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml, a spell dictionary, and a design doc. The cited login.ts:164-169 is actually the callbackPromise executor assigning callbackResolve/callbackReject. (3) The real callback handler (login.ts:168-182) parses only the code query param and 404s other paths; grep for state|timingSafeEqual across packages/cli/src shows no state/nonce read or comparison anywhere.
